(Neptune Beach, Florida) | college = *[[Tarleton State Texans men's basketball|Tarleton State]] (2022–2023) *[[Barton Cougars|Barton CC]] (2023–2024) *[[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]] (2024–2025) *[[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 54 | draft_team = [[Golden State Warriors]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | highlights = }} '''Lajae Leo Jones''' (born May 21, 2004) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tarleton State Texans men's basketball|Tarleton State Texans]], [[Barton Cougars]], [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure Bonnies]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. Jones was selected by the Warriors with the 54th pick in the second round of the [[2026 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Jones was born on May 21, 2004 to an [[African American]] father and an [[Israeli Jewish]] mother.[https://www.israelhayom.co.il/sport/world-basketball/article/20231612 Another step to the NBA: An impressive achievement for the Jewish college basketball player], [[Israel HaYom]], March 30th, 2026.{{Cite web|url=https://seminoles.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/lajae-jones/8041|publisher=[[Florida State Seminoles]]|title=Lajae Jones}} At age 13, his family moved to [[Neptune Beach, Florida]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/columns/ryan-o-halloran/2025/11/05/lajae-jones-florida-state-seminoles-basketball-acc-fletcher-high-school/87050170007/|newspaper=[[Florida Times-Union]]|title=FSU basketball's new look includes Lajae Jones, former Fletcher High star|author=O'Halloran, Ryan|date=November 5, 2025}} He attended [[Duncan U. Fletcher High School]] in Neptune Beach where he was a two-team all-conference selection and was named first-team all-state and the district player of the year as a [[Senior (education)|senior]]. A two-time team [[Captain (sports)|captain]], he averaged 20.7 points and 7.4 rebounds per game in his senior year. Jones had 1,426 points, 197 assists and 176 steals at Fletcher. He signed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Tarleton State Texans men's basketball|Tarleton State Texans]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/04/14/first-coast-varsity-weekly-lajae-jones-signs-tarleton-state-basketball/7306768001/|newspaper=[[Florida Times-Union]]|title=First Coast Varsity Weekly: Hoop dreams lead to Tarleton State for Fletcher's Lajae Jones|date=April 14, 2022|author=Freeman, Clayton}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] at Tarleton State in 2022–23, Jones appeared in 10 games, averaging 3.6 points and 1.4 rebounds. He transferred to [[Barton Community College]] in Kansas for the 2023–24 season, where he helped the team to a record of 36-1{{Cite web |title=Barton Cougars - Home of 62 National Championships |url=https://bartonsports.com/sports/mbkb/2023-24/teams/bartoncommunitycollege |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Barton Cougars - Home of 62 National Championships |language=en}} and won the [[junior college]] national championship, averaging 15.4 points and 9.2 rebounds per game. Jones transferred again after the season to the [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure Bonnies]], playing a year there and starting 33 games.{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25445283-warriors-draft-lajae-jones-watch-highlights-no-54-pick-2026-nba-draft|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|title=Warriors Draft Lajae Jones, Watch Highlights of No. 54 Pick in 2026 NBA Draft|author=Peters, Andrew|date=June 24, 2026}} For the Bonnies, Jones shot 45.6 percent from the field and posted averages of 10.8 points and 5.8 rebounds.{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2025/03/31/fsu-basketball-lajae-jones-st-bonaventure-ncaa-transfer-portal/82739840007/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=FSU basketball lands St. Bonaventure transfer Lajae Jones from NCAA transfer portal|author=Holland Jr., Peter|date=March 31, 2025}} He transferred a third time in 2025, joining the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]], where he averaged 12.7 points and 5.7 rebounds in his lone season there.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/golden-state-warriors-select-florida-state-s-22318130.php|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|title=Warriors again seek size, add 6-foot-7 guard Lajae Jones in second round of NBA draft|author=Kroichick, Ron|date=June 24, 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 24, 2026, Jones was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 54th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=|first=|title=Warriors Select Lajae Jones With 54th Overall Pick in the 2026 Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/videos/warriors-select-lajae-jones-with-54th-overall-pick-in-the-2026-draft|work=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026}} On 2 July, 2026, he was announced to participate with the team during the [[2026 NBA Summer League]], along with fellow draftee [[Yaxel Lendeborg]] ([[2026 NBA Draft|2026]] No. 11 pick).{{Cite web|title= Warriors Announce Gold and Blue Rosters for California Classic |url= https://warriors.com/news/warriors-announce-gold-and-blue-rosters-for-california-classic-20260702 |website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2026|access-date=July 2, 2026}} On July 19, 2026, Jones, alongside the Warriors, won the [[2026 NBA Summer League|2026 NBA Summer League Championship]] against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], where in 11 minutes, he scored 4 points in a 94–90 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer-league/boxscore/_/gameId/401881722/league/nba-summer-las-vegas|title=Warriors 94-90 Grizzlies (Jul 19, 2026) Final Score |website=[[ESPN]] |date=July 19, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}} Following the Summer League conclusion, Jones averaged 8.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 0.4 assists in 16.3 minutes.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Golden-State-Warriors/9/Rosters/Summer_League|title=2026 Warriors 2026 NBA Summer League Stats|website=[[RealGM]] |date=July 21, 2026 |access-date=July
